title: Both IPv6 and IPv4 IP addresses in a single connect token?

nodes.body:
Can confirm this workaround solution is not secure. The real solution I think is to add first class support for dual ipv4 and ipv6 sockets inside the netcode_socket_t implementation. eg. create two sockets internally, one for ipv4 and one for ipv6. This way it would pass up to yojimbo, perhaps with some changed signature, eg. you have to pass the ipv4 and the ipv6 bind addresses vs. just one or the other.

I feel this would be a lot of work, but it definitely seems the right approach.

Seems best to approach this by making changes and proving it out in netcode.io first, and then porting up to yojimbo.

Thoughts?

That makes sense, it's something that we'll hopefully have time to work on done the road. Thanks for the advice.

Just a heads up, it turns out that while the hybrid IPv4/IPv6 socket works on Android and Linux, it is not supported on iOS. Instead we've implemented a solution higher up and mostly outside of Yojimbo/Netcode to manage IPv4 vs IPv6.

The final addition we had to implement for the above was to expose the client address and change the address from ipv4 to ipv6 (and back), while overwriting server_addresses that do not match the ip format in `netcode_read_connect_token`. 

If we add an appropriate whitelist back in would this approach be secure?

I think the ultimate correct approach here, is that netcode.io servers should simultaneously support connection via IPv6 or IPv4 at the user's discretion.

I think such a change is a perfect feature addition, and it definitely should be done.

Calling out to everybody out there, what is the best way for us to do this, should we have multiple sockets per-netcode.io server, eg. one for ipv4 an one for ipv6, or should this be done some other way?

In other words, what is the best practice for a server that has to accept UDP packets from both IPv4 and IPv6 in 2018?

cheers

- Glenn
ps. I'm very interested in adding this, but right now I'm also very busy with my new startup. If anybody wants to have a crack at this, I'm happy to review the changes.

Sounds good. I've actually been working on getting a solution for this ready. I'd like to get some thorough testing completed on the changes before push anything up. I should have a PR up this coming week.

I have a suggestion, for backwards compatibility, could you implement it without changing the signature.

For example, when passing in addresses, use the form:

"[ipv4]|[ipv6]"

For example:

"127.0.0.1|::1"

This would retain compatibility with yojimbo, which uses netcode.io, and make the functionality you add work for people who use yojimbo without any changes.

Of course, you should still support single addresses, but add the "x|y" format to support up to two sockets per-client/server.

cheers

- Glenn
And of course, please extend the tests to have a test case with your addition!

Alright. I put [this](https://github.com/networkprotocol/netcode.io/pull/60) PR up. It's got the support for passing 2 addresses & creating 2 sockets when creating the server and the client. 

I added a decent description covering the changes, but you might find the test cases to be a bit much based on the testing that was previously incorporated. 

Obviously the Travis build failed. I already tried to get that passing a few times, but the tests aren't failing for me locally. Maybe you could point me in the right direction. Otherwise, I'll take a look tomorrow. 

As far as implementation goes, the changes are backwards compatible as I made sure not to change the signatures for `netcode_client_create` & `netcode_server_create`. I've allowed the ipv4/ ipv6 addresses to be passed in in any order (or in theory 2 ipv4/6's). Most of the actual functionality testing I did was on our internal fork of yojimbo, which obviously doesn't point at exactly the same commit, but the implementation matches.

Let me know if you require any changes.

**THIS IS FANTASTIC!**

What OS are you developing on? Try running the tests under Linux?
ps. Good call on the any order for addresses. Excellent
ps. If you don't have easy access to linux (eg. developing under Mac, Windows), try running a plain docker ubuntu instance. Really easy to test under there. That's how I do it.

Tests are passing. For some reason it wasn't able to bind to the ipv6 loopback in the `test_client_create` suite. Maybe you can enlighten me as to why. 

Hopefully you could leave any comments or approval you see fit on the PR and we can move forward from there.
I've noticed IPv6 weirdness in Travis too. I don't think it's you. I think it's however they've setup the networking for those VMs. Nice find. Accepting pull request now. Nice work!
